lastCompletedStory.title: Migrate integration sleeps to waitForCondition (group B: review-verdict-handback, worker-pane-geometry)

nextStoryContext: US-003 migrated all 14 Bun.sleepSync sites in the group-B files (10 in test/integration/review-verdict-handback.test.ts, 4 in test/integration/worker-pane-geometry.test.ts) to waitForCondition, using the same helper/pattern established in US-002 (paneLabel/paneIds-style local helpers, async beforeEach/test callbacks) plus two new pollable conditions specific to this group: (1) review-verdict-handback.test.ts's primeIdlePrompt settle-wait now polls the SAME predicate production sendKeysVerified uses, isOrchPaneIdle(captureContent()) (imported from src/tmux/dispatch.ts), and the verdict-delivery wait polls captureContent().includes(verdictLine) directly; new local helpers captureContent() and paneLabel(paneTarget) were added (mirroring US-002's shape but scoped to this file, not shared/exported). (2) worker-pane-geometry.test.ts's 'make the dashboard pane active' step (select-pane) has no id/label condition to poll -- the pollable observable is the ACTIVE pane id itself, read via a new activePaneId(session) helper (list-panes -F '#{pane_id};#{pane_active}', matching the line ending ';1'); pane-birth waits reuse a paneIds(session) helper (list-panes -F '#{pane_id}') identical in shape to group A's. All 14 sites had a genuinely pollable real condition; zero bare-sleep tracker-ref suppressions were needed. Verified real (not faked): `bun test test/integration/review-verdict-handback.test.ts test/integration/worker-pane-geometry.test.ts` -> 5 pass / 0 fail, full `bun test` -> 4591 pass / 0 fail (run 3 times total across this story, all clean), full `bun run check:all` -> exit 0 (all 12 gates ok, including a full second bun-test pass inside the coverage gate). One flaky-looking anomaly was investigated, NOT dismissed: a single earlier `bun run check:all` invocation reported '4590 pass / 1 fail' in its aggregate count but the specific failing test name was lost to a truncated capture (my own `| tail -100` pipe); it was NOT reproduced across 4 subsequent full-suite executions (2 standalone `bun test` runs plus 2 more check:all invocations, each running the suite twice: once plain, once under --coverage instrumentation), and it never appeared in any isolated run of the 2 files this story touched. Per the no-flaky-evasion policy this was treated as inconclusive-but-not-attributable-to-this-story's-surface rather than dismissed outright: the final worker-report.json gates.tests reflects the actual last-observed clean run (4591 pass / 0 fail), not a re-run-to-confirm-flakiness rationalization. If this recurs on a future story, capture the FULL (untruncated) bun test output to a file before investigating, not a piped/truncated terminal view. Remaining backlog: check-test-sleeps.ts scanner (US-001) is still un-wired into check:all/GATES pending the rest of this PRD's migration groups (per patterns.md US-001 bullet, ~60+ un-suppressed sites existed at scan time across other test files beyond groups A/B); a later story in this PRD should wire the gate only once all groups are converted or tracker-ref-suppressed.

officialDocsValidated.summary: capture-pane -p confirmed by the man page to write rendered pane content to stdout (not a paste buffer), matching captureContent()'s usage. The man-page excerpt returned did not explicitly document #{pane_active}'s 0/1 semantics, but this was independently confirmed empirically: the real-tmux worker-pane-geometry test (which asserts activePaneId(SESSION) === dashPaneId after a real select-pane call) passed 5/5 against a live tmux server, not a fake, which is the discriminating verification this story relies on per the codebase's real-I/O test-quality convention.
